nodes.text: Is it true that, for every prime $p$, there is a prime $q<p$ which is a primitive root modulo $p$?

#985 : [Er65b] number theory Artin conjectured that $2$ is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$, which Hooley [Ho67b] proved assuming the Generalised Riemann Hypothesis. Heath-Brown [He86b] proved that at least one of $2$, $3$, or $5$ is a primitive root for infinitely many primes $p$.
